Stuffing cotton balls into a perfectly good whisk and saying that's upcycling?

"Upcycling" includes reusing something for a purpose other than its originally intended purpose (repurposing). If someone doesn't have a way to store their cotton balls outside of the bag they came in, and they don't want to leave that on the counter, who am I to deem the solution to their problem as any less "upcycling" than upcycling/repurposing old tires into shoes?

Punching holes into perfectly good kitchen utensils and saying you're re-purposing them?

If they're used for something other than their intended purpose, it definitely is repurposing the item by definition. Now, would I want to waste a perfectly good kettle? No. But I also don't have five kettles sitting around my house. I have one. Would I use 30 metal spatulas to make a lamp shade if I had them dropped into my lap? Probably not, but it's a great idea (for example) at reusing something for an alternative purpose and doesn't result in the objects going into a landfill.
